newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister begins key talks with metalworkers.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister begins key talks with metalworkers.

text.p: Labour Minister Tiziano Treu began a crucial meeting with Italian engineering and metalworkers' trades unions in a bid to end a bitter dispute over wage contracts.
After the talks with the FIOM, FIM and UILM unions, representing some 1.5 million workers, Treu is due to meet employers group Federmeccanica.
Treu said on Wednesday he hoped the two sides could reach an accord by Christmas as he stepped in to mediate after months of deadlock.
Union-employer contracts expired in June. The unions recently held two national strikes in support of their claim for wage rises for the 1997-98 contractual period.
In cash terms, unions want a gross 262,000 lire ($170) rise in monthly pay packets, of which 97,000 lire is to cover an overshoot in real against targeted inflation between 1994-96.
Employers say the claim is excessive and have offered a total 195,000 lire of which 30,000 is for inflation.
Even the Bank of Italy said in its October economic review said the workers' claims "do not fully take into account the falling trend in inflation."
Inflation in Italy fell to its lowest rate for 27 years in November, according to figures released earlier on Thursday.
The national statistics office ISTAT said consumer price inflation last month was 2.6 percent year-on-year, down from 3.0 percent in October and 6.0 percent in November 1995.
It was the lowest since June 1969, when the figure was 2.5 percent.
